en: The *Buddhagaṇḍīstava*,
composed by the master Aśvaghoṣa:
He who, formerly at the foot of the Bodhi tree on the path of the sun’s course, [subdued] the dances and songs of Māra...

May the Lion of the Śākyas, who is saluted by gods and men, protect you— he who was never shaken from his composure by women of celestial form, even when they incessantly uttered the soft, double-syllabled mantras "gaṃgau gaṃgau gagaṃgau" and "ghaghanaghanam," and by those drums that were difficult to break and difficult to endure. || 1 ||
He who is [known] by the "ka-ka-ha-ka-ha-ka-ha" and "hā-hā-hā" laughter of the women of Kandarpa; by the "taṭiti," "taṭa-taṭa," and "tātaṭī" outcries of those with vast pomp;
and by the words of the servants, "kut-kut," "budbuda," "kukūcit," and "kuha-kuha-kuha."
May that Lord of Sages, who is gentle, whose every blemish has been washed away by sacred learning, and who is the source of all brilliance, be for your peace.

With the casting of eyebrows and the arching of outer corners of the eyes; with glances from eyes whose lashes and pupils shimmer like the arrows of Love; with limbs that enact the playful dance of graceful vine-like arms;
and with bashful, smiling words, sweet and soft with a gentle fragrance— [The hearts of the world are captivated by these mature women of love.]
Salutations to him, by whom even the mind has been rendered free from delusion—he who has conquered the power of Smara. || 3 ||
Shaking the broad earth, covering the sky with multitudes of sharp arrows,
causing the ten directions to blaze with the flames of the fire of their wrath, and agitating the ocean;
the heroic Māra warriors resounded with the sharp clanging of swords, discuses, and saws brandished with ease.
May that Lord of Sages protect you, by whom [the hosts] were forcibly conquered with the weapon of loving-kindness. || 4 ||
Terrible with the roar of a manifest, formidable display of wrath thundering forth;
creating darkness by the massed pride of herds of elephants resembling a network of roaring clouds;
and illuminating the entire universe with the rays of the flashing sword that was like the fierce fire of Kandarpa.
May that Buddha protect you, by whom the vast army of the Flower-Arrowed One was instantly shattered. || 5 ||
With divine, ear-reaching, lotus-petal-like eyes— possessing thick lashes, tremulous pupils, moist with emotion, skillful, moving gracefully, accompanied by smiles,
and adorned with playful arches of the brows— the restless, red-cornered glances of the women of Māra surrounded [him].
I bow to that best of sages, who has cast out all defects and who cannot be led astray in any way whatsoever.

He whose mind was not agitated by Māras— those with tongues flickering amidst their thick, formidable manes, holding spears in their hands, with faces like elephants, horses, lions, and tigers; he by whom Pradyumna, the god of love, who fears such fury, was disregarded as if he were a blade of grass.
May the Fully Awakened One, the Lord of the World, the Sovereign of Sages, who is free from all defilement, protect you. (7)

He whose intellect is unshakable, even by the infinite, roaring, and terrible Māra-soldiers— who possess hundreds of various faces and resemble the waters of mountains, rivers, oceans, and clouds— by him, the All-Knowing One free from passion, that Puṣpaketu was disregarded like a blade of grass.
May that glorious Hero among Buddhas, the remover of the fear of defilement and free from passion, protect you. (8)

The mind of him whose firm cross-legged posture remained undisturbed— unshakable like a mountain— even by the most fierce female Māras with hands grasping swords, axes, bows, spears, and tridents, and by many terrifying, deep, and sharp-sounding roars like falling meteors; [He is the one who, having attained the supreme state, will teach the Dharma.]
I pay homage to that hero among Buddhas, the preeminent hero, worthy of veneration, who removes the fear of the three realms of existence. 9.

Even with their high-pitched, loud laughter, with bells fastened to their manifest and skillful warriors, with their matted locks tangled and bursting with the sound of arrogant slapping, and with their hollow-eyed servants ringing their gongs—
those who were unable to break his awakening by the vigorous beating of sharp drums and cymbals; [He is the one whose awakening could not be disturbed even by such forces.]
May that Hero among Buddhas, who was as skillful as a sharp drum upon Vulture Peak for the sake of the arrogant, be for your benefit. || 10 ||
Kokaṇḍa, Rāmakaṇḍa, Pratibhayakuhara, Darpadarpa, Raṇāṇḍa, Ḍimba, Ḍimba, Ḍaḍimba, Ḍuha, Ḍuhaka, Ḍuha, Tṛṃkhala,
Tṛṃkhala, Tṛm, Jhimba, Jhimba, Jhajhimba, Khamu, Khamu, Khamukha, Maṃkhu, Maṃkhuḥ, Khumaṃkhu—
Unafraid by these roars, the Lion of the Śākyas, saluted by the best of gods, may he protect you. || 11 ||

At night, the splendor of perfect enlightenment— whose sole partisan was opposed to the beauty of the forest of lotus-faces of the Māra-maidens, and who was joined with the intense onset of the vow that bore a shower of embers for Māra— attained him, just as the autumnal moonlight reaches the moon.
This is the gong of the Blessed One, the King of Dharma; it resounds as his messenger of the Dharma.

Since Death, whose end is never seen, slays even for a moment after a long wait— yet those whose minds are cast upon that which is difficult to endure [worldly things] must at all times show devotion to virtuous deeds;
thus does this [Dharma], which repeatedly speaks as if it were the command of the Three Jewels to living beings, [protect them].
This is the gong of the Dharma, resounding loudly and making the entire circle of the quarters famous with its noise. || 13 ||
Having conquered the host of heretics like the orb of the sun conquers the multitude of stars, the teaching of the Jina shines here;
it brings great joy to the ornament of the earth’s surface.
The gaṇḍī is as fierce as the victory drum of Yama. || 14 ||
That which possesses absolute firmness— *jami jami*, *ḍuḍubham*, *rañjitena alinālim*, *ḍimbam ḍimbam*, *ḍiḍimbam*, *ḍubhaḍubhaḍuḍubham*,
*nāḍivan nāḍibhaṇḍam*, *ruṇḍam ruṇḍam*, *ruruṇḍam*, *yaralava*, *khakhumam*, *maṃkhumaṃkhuḥ*, *khumaṃkhuḥ*.
Behold, in this world of living beings, the army of Māra is being crushed by the One who possesses the power of the ten strengths.
The king of mountains, Meru, trembles as the earth shakes from the upheaval of an earthquake; the hosts of gods, along with the multitudes of planets and all the kings of the nāgas,
are terrified upon hearing the fierce ghaṇṭā, which causes manifold fear and strikes terror into the heretics.
For the sake of peace for the Buddhists, it immediately resounds, making the earth ring out as if it were crying aloud. || 16 ||
This gong resounds upon the pinnacle of the monastery,
producing delightful sounds with the resonance of thunder; like a mother out of affection for her children, it calls out to those who have gone far away.
The gong at mealtime calls the sons together.
The sound of the Buddha— who is intent upon turning the wheel of saṃsāra and who is adorned with the jewels of all virtues—
is like the resonance of a celestial drum.
The gong wards off all misfortunes. || 18 ||
For this gong resounds to awaken men, gods, humans, and asuras;
O noble ones, listen to the gong of the Sugata!
It was filled with complete assemblies of monks. || 19 ||
Where, even today, do people— trembling with fear at the suspicion of its destruction— scatter serpents into the sky like clouds agitated at the time of universal dissolution,
seeking a remedy for that [sound] which still resounds, having quelled the pride of all rival sectarians?
May that gaṇḍī gong, established by all the supreme sages for the increase of the Dharma, protect you all. (20)
This ghaṇṭā of the Tathāgata— who is honored by gods, asuras, and great nāgas, and who has attained supreme peace—
resounds with a voice like the drum of the immortals.
Tearing asunder the hearts of the followers of other sects. || 21 ||
"O people, be intent upon merit which bestows heaven and liberation;
do not commit sin, which brings about miserable rebirths. Life is fickle! Thus, with effort, I restrained those whose cries were like the humming of bees settled in the midst [of the flowers]."
May this handful of flowers offered at the lotus feet of the Enemy of Māra protect you. || 22 ||

As he was descending from heaven to earth, Indra and the hosts of gods, led by Śakra, respectfully followed him for a long time, scattering flowers, filling the quarters with the sounds of musical instruments, and preceded by shouts of "Jojoka!"— so it is said.
May the fierce gong of that Blessed One, the ocean of compassion, protect the world.
Having taken seven steps immediately upon emerging from his mother’s womb, he—who possessed no other thought—spontaneously uttered the words, "This is mine: the cessation of the stream of saṃsāra.
Furthermore, it was he to whom the self-born Brahmā proclaimed the radiant three worlds.
May that Gaṇḍī of the Victorious Sugata, which shatters the darkness, be for you. 24.
Having conquered the host of Māra, which causes great terror, and having brought about the destruction of all faults,
he attained that most beautiful state of omniscience right there on the outskirts during that very night. To that Buddha, the wise one whose nature is pure and who is a mine of all virtues—
May the Gaṇḍī, which destroys fierce and fragmented sins, lead men to prosperity. || 25 ||
Brahmā became as if dejected; the Preceptor of the Gods entirely abandoned his pride; Śiva’s mind was shrunken, and the Lord Viṣṇu remained silent.
Thus, when his virtues were being proclaimed, the gods fell into a state of mute silence out of shame.
May this gong of that Sage be victorious for you, and may it protect the world from the lower realms. || 26 ||
Brahmā, Āditya, Śaśāṅka, Śaṅkara, Śatākṣa, Upendra, Yakṣas, and others; Gandharvas, Uragas, Kinnaras, Asuras, Samīras, Pretas, Pīḍās, and Ambareśas—
whatever immortals dwell there, as well as humans on the surface of the earth and in the worlds of the nether regions (pātāla).
Let all of you come together to hear this Dharma from the Teacher, the Tathāgata. || 27 ||
At her birth, the non-Buddhist heretics, their minds debased and inferior, were overcome with grief;
the Buddhists, their intellects nourished by an extraordinary height of joy, attained steadfastness.
Having encountered her, virtues expand to their full extent and faults come to an end.
May that Gaṇḍī-bell, which removes the defilement of the Kali age, lead to your prosperity. || 28 ||
Having bowed according to the rules to that [Dharma-gong] of the Sage, those of purified intellect attain the exalted state;
and all adversaries, rendered powerless, go swiftly to their destruction.
That Dharma-gong of the Sage has shattered and scattered the entire veil of delusion.
May it arise for you, long-lived ones, to dispel the fear born of worldly existence. 29.
Upon hearing it, Brahmā and the other gods fell to the surface of the earth; the inhabitants of heaven tremble, the mountains shake, and even the earth quickly sank into the depths of the underworld.
This [teaching], which strikes fear into the heretics, was proclaimed by one whose soul was purified by the undertaking of the welfare of others.
Let that drumstick be struck immediately for the sake of the Buddhists' pacification. || 30 ||
Mounted upon the mature [Gaurī] in the *ālīḍha* posture, his heavy foot treading upon the tips of Gaurī’s breasts;
the upper body of the All-Knowing One, roaring with hundreds of clearly manifest and formidable [mantras];
his limbs blazing with a garland of flames; terrifying with the *huṃkāra* that pervades the hollows of the three worlds.
Victorious is he whose crown is bound with both the bound and the unbound—the sun and moon among gods, humans, and lords of asuras. || 31 ||
With the rhythmic clapping of hands by those passionate women— deer-eyed, possessing full and lofty breasts, and moving with the graceful gait of swans—
the air resounds on all sides with songs and instrumental music, uttering "daṃ daṃ daṃ daṃ da daṃ daṃ tani tani tanita" and "tuṃ tuṃ tuṃ tuṃ tatuṃ tuṃ."
"Ṭuṃ ṭuṃ ṭuṃ ṭuṃ ṭuṭuṃ ṭuṃ ṭum—thus is this ghaṇṭikā struck with measured rhythm. (32)
The *Buddhagaṇḍī* is completed.
This is the work of the venerable teacher Ācārya Śrī Aśvaghoṣa.
